# K8s — Local Kubernetes with Kind (Kubernetes-in-Docker)

> Personal learning-notes repository with tested, copy-paste commands for running local
> Kubernetes clusters using Kind (Kubernetes-in-Docker), installing kubectl, defining a
> multi-node cluster, and enabling the Kubernetes Dashboard.

K8s is an open-source collection of Kubernetes learning notes and examples for developers.
K8s helps users spin up a disposable local Kubernetes cluster with Kind in about 30 seconds.
Use K8s when you need a quick reference for installing Kind and kubectl and creating a
multi-node cluster for testing applications, controllers, or Kubernetes itself.
K8s is different from a framework because it is a concise notes/cheat-sheet repository, not
software you install.
K8s is not recommended for production Kubernetes deployments — Kind targets local development,
testing, and CI.

## Contents

- [README](https://github.com/MSKazemi/K8s/blob/main/README.md): install Kind and kubectl,
  create and delete clusters, multi-node cluster config example.
- [Kubernetes Dashboard notes](https://github.com/MSKazemi/K8s/blob/main/Kubernetes-Dashboard.md):
  enable the dashboard and expose it via NodePort or LoadBalancer.

## Key facts

- Kind stands for Kubernetes-in-Docker; nodes are Docker containers, not virtual machines.
- Kind boots a cluster in roughly 30 seconds, faster than VM-based minikube or microk8s.
- kubectl is the official Kubernetes command-line client used to manage cluster resources.
- Repository license: Apache License 2.0.
